title: The Data Context Layer for Agents — Yoni Michael & Brandon Callender, Typedef
talk_summary: Typedef argues agents fail on data/code tasks because key semantics—grain, join safety, metric meaning, dependencies—are not queryable, so they build a deterministic context graph refreshed incrementally and queried by agents. The workshop shows a code graph can cut tokens and improve consistency, but the main lesson is that agents often ignore new tools unless you design tools around model reflexes and measure adoption with evals.

takeaways.what_they_do: Parse code deterministically into symbols and typed edges, resolve identities, store them in a graph, and let the agent query the needed subgraph instead of re-reading the repo.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to always be as deterministic as possible first and then only use LLMs when you're trying to resolve ambiguity
takeaways.numbers: Task success ~35 points higher with context layer; graph agent used ~3.1x fewer tokens; pass^k twice as good in their eval

takeaways.what_they_do: Use fixed-snapshot eval corpora, deterministic scoring, repeated runs, pass@k and pass^k, and explicitly measure whether the agent calls the new tools; read traces before trusting scores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an elegant tool that gets reached for a third of the time is just a third of a tool
takeaways.numbers: Tool usage 34% -> 72% after prompt change; pass^k graph agent twice as good; ~3.1x fewer tokens

takeaways.technique: Design tools to match model reflexes
takeaways.what_they_do: Name the graph tool “search,” accept multi-keyword queries, and return ripgrep-like results so the model uses familiar patterns; ensure the first call returns useful results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you call a tool search, the agent will basically always do multi keyword search into it

takeaways.technique: Evidence store plus small LLM passes
takeaways.what_they_do: Persist deterministic facts and small auditable LLM summaries per symbol/column; ask many focused questions instead of one big prompt.
Compute the graph once, refresh it atomically/incrementally on commits, and design incremental indexing as a first-class requirement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: design for incremental indexing first as a first class citizen

takeaways.what_they_do: Before editing, walk downstream dependencies to identify affected symbols/dashboards and flag semantic or grain changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it knows a blast radius before it actually even acts on it
takeaways.numbers: Task success ~35 points higher with context layer
